messages:
sam: quick heads-up — after the kernel-route tweak this morning we're seeing microburst OOMs when batches hydrate heavy KV items. repro on canary:

sam: profiling snapshot:
```
GPU mem usage spike -> 95% after batch formation
KV cache resident: 2.8GB (limit 3.0GB)
batch_token_budget: 2048 -> actual aggregated tokens 3100
kernel_route: fast-attn-v2
```

anya: :eyes: do we have batch admission trimming in the new path?

sam: admission runs, but it uses per-request token cap only. it doesn't account KV footprint. so when multiple requests with long cache prefixes join, we exceed headroom.

kai: maybe add an estimated_kv_bytes per request and gate admission by headroom_estimate? we discussed approx calculation last quarter.

ops: what about fallback kernel? can we route to compact-kernel when kv pressure high?

sam: fallback exists but not triggered — kernel selection is locked earlier based on seq_len and latency SLO, before kv-estimate is applied.

anya: suggestion: move kv_headroom check into early admission stage and reduce batch token budget dynamically. pseudo:
```
if total_est_kv + current_kv > kv_limit * 0.9:
    reduce batch_token_budget *= 0.6
    deny new long-prefix requests
```

kai: sounds good. also add a fast estimator using prefix_hash -> kv_entry_size map to avoid per-request scan.

infra-bot: deploy canary scheduled to 5398765500 (shepherder-kv-estimator-0.1)

sam: I'll prototype estimator + early admission hook. will post perf numbers once canary runs. thanks.

anya: ty! keep an eye on latency p50/p95 when shrinking budgets.

ops: if canary shows regression, auto-fallback to previous admission rules at +10% error rate.

sam: noted. will update.
